headline: Connecting to consumer Gmail requires a strict verification process and a mandatory third-party security assessment, taking upwards of 6 weeks for production access.
summary: To read emails and send replies on behalf of external users, your app must undergo Google's mandatory brand and scope verification, plus an annual CASA (Cloud Application Security Assessment) audit. Testing can begin immediately for up to 100 pre-approved test users. Using user email content for generalized AI/ML foundation model training is strictly forbidden.

oauth.pkce: Supported and recommended (S256); required for public clients.
oauth.refresh_tokens: Requires access_type=offline and prompt=consent on first auth. Expires in 7 days for apps in Testing status, or after 6 months of inactivity in production.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Requires exact character matching. Must use https:// for production web clients (no HTTP, wildcards, URL fragments, or query parameters). http://localhost and http://127.0.0.1 with any port are permitted for local testing.
oauth.scopes: Requests must be exactly scoped to least privilege. Using broad scopes like mail.google.com or gmail.modify when gmail.send and gmail.readonly suffice will lead to rejection.

steps.title: Create project and configure test OAuth screen
steps.detail: Create a project in the Google Cloud Console, enable the Gmail API, and configure the OAuth consent screen. Set the user type to 'External' and status to 'Testing'. Add up to 100 specific Google accounts to the test users list.

steps.title: Test endpoints and generate URLs
steps.detail: Construct the exact OAuth authorization URLs with PKCE S256 and required scopes for the local test environment.

steps.title: Update legal and compliance policies
steps.detail: Update the app's privacy policy to explicitly state compliance with Google's Limited Use policy (including no AI/ML foundation model training on emails) and include data deletion instructions.

steps.title: Verify domains
steps.detail: Verify the domains hosting your homepage, privacy policy, and terms of service in Google Search Console using the same Google Cloud account.

steps.title: Record YouTube demo video
steps.detail: Record a demo video demonstrating the full OAuth flow. The OAuth client ID must be clearly readable in the browser address bar. Demonstrate the exact features utilizing the requested Gmail scopes.

steps.title: Draft scope justification
steps.detail: Write the justification demonstrating why gmail.readonly and gmail.send are the minimum required scopes for the app's functionality.

steps.title: Submit for brand and sensitive scope review
steps.detail: Submit the app for verification in Google Cloud Console. Brand review takes 2-3 days, and sensitive scope review takes up to 10 business days.

steps.title: Undergo CASA Security Assessment
steps.detail: Because gmail.readonly is a restricted scope and user data leaves Google's servers, you must pass an annual Cloud Application Security Assessment (CASA Tier 2 / 3) conducted by an authorized independent lab to receive a Letter of Assessment.

requirements.text: The app's homepage, privacy policy, and terms of service must reside on domains verified in Google Search Console under the same developer account.
The privacy policy must explicitly disclose compliance with Google's Limited Use policy and state that email data will not be used for generalized AI/ML foundation model training.
Apps requesting restricted scopes like gmail.readonly must complete a mandatory third-party CASA security assessment and receive an LOA.
Google's OIDC discovery and authorization endpoints natively support standard PKCE with the S256 method.

gotchas.text: Refresh tokens expire automatically after 7 days if the OAuth consent screen is left in 'Testing' mode.

If moved to 'In production' without completing verification, external users encounter an 'unsafe' warning and the app is limited to a lifetime cap of 100 new user grants before authentication is permanently disabled.
Submitting a demo video where the OAuth Client ID is obscured or missing from the browser URL bar will cause immediate rejection.
Failure to respond to Trust & Safety clarification questions within 90 days results in automatic rejection and closure of the verification ticket.

The gmail.modify scope combines read, compose, and send privileges, but requesting it instead of separate restricted scopes may lead to rejection for over-scoping if full modification isn't justified.

permissions.review_impact: This is a Restricted scope requiring rigorous brand verification, Limited Use policy compliance, and a mandatory annual third-party CASA security assessment (which incurs assessor fees).
This is a Sensitive scope requiring brand verification, a verified domain, a compliant privacy policy, and a demo video, but not a CASA assessment on its own.

blockers.issue: Refresh tokens for test users are unexpectedly invalidating after 7 days.
blockers.how_to_proceed: This is expected behavior for apps in 'Testing' status. To bypass the 7-day expiry, either move the app to 'In production' (which imposes a 100-user lifetime cap until verified) or periodically re-authenticate test users.

blockers.issue: OAuth app rejected for over-scoped permissions.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Downgrade the requested scopes to the absolute minimum (e.g., from mail.google.com to gmail.readonly and gmail.send) and rewrite your written justification detailing why the specific features strictly require these exact scopes.

agent_can: Draft the Limited Use clause and data deletion language for your privacy policy
Write the formal least privilege justification for the gmail.readonly and gmail.send scopes
Configure local OAuth testing code with correct PKCE and redirect URI parameters
Monitor rate limits against the 250 units/second and 1B units/day thresholds
you_must: Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console
Record and upload the YouTube demo video showing the client ID in the URL bar and the scopes in action
Submit the app for verification in Google Cloud Console
Contract an authorized third-party lab and pay for the annual CASA security assessment

key_claims.text: The authorization endpoint and Google Cloud developer portal are active and enforcing client validations.
Google charges no fees for the verification review itself, but third-party labs charge for the CASA assessment.
Internal Workspace apps restricted solely to users within a single tenant are exempt from OAuth verification and user limits.
Reading a message costs 5 quota units; sending a reply costs 100 quota units.

open_questions: Exact cost of the required CASA Tier 2 / 3 assessment, as authorized labs set their own pricing based on architecture.
assumptions: Hands-on time is an estimate based on standard development tasks (domain verification, drafting policies, recording video).
Time to first connection assumes the developer immediately sets up a test app and authenticates their own test user account.
Approval wait of 6+ weeks is based on Google's stated official timeline for restricted scope verification, but can take longer depending on responsiveness and CASA audit duration.
